Most importantly, routing using traffic data means that ABRP routing will only believe a road is viable if someone in their dataset has driven it recently. Elsewise ABRP treats the road as closed, which means routing fundamentally breaks in rural areas. You can turn off traffic data, but only temporarily. Having it off means you get navigated into traffic jams. ABRP refuses to fix this problem and others.

content: Tried ABRP with an OBD dongle on a 2000-km road trip. It refused to plot routes near my range limit, opting for longer, unnecessary detours to even more distant chargers. Despite real-time OBD data, it miscalculated range, predicting negative battery until 50 km from a charger. Interface was buggy, crashing on my Fold 6, formatting badly on Android Auto unless maximized. Frustrated, I relied on Google Maps and mental math for better accuracy. ABRP’s hype doesn’t match its failure-prone reality.
